questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which living thing in an Australian bushland is a producer?
questions.explanation: A gum tree makes its own food using sunlight. Animals have to eat to get food.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Mushrooms grow on a dead log in the forest. They break the log down into tiny pieces. What are mushrooms in this habitat?
questions.explanation: Decomposers break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Here is a food chain: grass → grasshopper → lizard → hawk. Which living thing is a producer?
questions.explanation: Grass makes its own food. The other three eat to get their food.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: In a food chain, an arrow points from a rosella to a falcon. What does the arrow show?
choices: The falcon is eaten by the rosella
The rosella is bigger than the falcon
Food and energy pass from the rosella to the falcon
The falcon makes food for the rosella
questions.explanation: The arrow points to the eater. The falcon eats the rosella and gets its energy.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: On a farm, the food chain is grass → rabbit → fox. Most of the foxes leave the farm. What will most likely happen to the rabbits?
choices: The rabbits will start to eat foxes
questions.explanation: Fewer foxes means fewer rabbits get eaten, so the number of rabbits goes up.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Water vapour rises high in the air and cools. It turns into tiny drops that make clouds. What is this stage called?
questions.explanation: When water vapour cools and turns back into liquid drops, it is called condensation.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: After rain, a puddle is on the school playground. On a hot day the puddle disappears. Where did the water go?
choices: It went into the air as water vapour
It froze and stayed on the ground
It was used up and is gone forever
questions.explanation: The Sun's heat makes the water evaporate. It goes into the air as water vapour.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A farmer in outback Queensland pumps water from a bore. Where does the bore water come from?
choices: From melted snow on the farm
questions.explanation: A bore is a deep hole that reaches water stored under the ground.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What gives the energy that makes water evaporate in the water cycle?
questions.explanation: The Sun's heat warms water so it can change into water vapour.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Rain falls on hills and runs into creeks. The creeks flow into a river and then into the sea. What is this stage of the water cycle called?
questions.explanation: Collection is when water gathers in creeks, rivers, lakes and the sea.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Mia pushes a toy car across the carpet and then across the tiles. It rolls much further on the tiles. Why?
questions.explanation: Smooth tiles have less friction than carpet, so the car slows down less.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A mango falls from a tree to the ground. Which force pulls it down?
questions.explanation: Gravity is the pull that draws objects towards the Earth.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Sam has a magnet. Which of these will it pick up?
questions.explanation: Magnets attract objects made of iron or steel. Wood, plastic and glass are not attracted.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Jo squeezes the brakes on her bike. The brake pads rub on the wheel and the bike slows down. Which force slows the wheel?
questions.explanation: Rubbing surfaces make friction. Friction slows moving things down.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A magnet can pull on a steel nail without touching it.
questions.explanation: Magnetic force works across a gap, so a magnet can pull a nail from a short distance.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which of these is a natural material that comes from a plant?
questions.explanation: Cotton comes from the cotton plant. Nylon, plastic and glass are made in factories.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Windows in a house are made of glass. Which quality of glass makes it good for windows?
questions.explanation: Glass is clear, so light comes in and people can see outside.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Electrical wires have a copper metal core. Why is copper used?
choices: It lets electricity flow through it easily
questions.explanation: Metals like copper carry electricity well, so they are good for wires.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A raincoat is made from plastic. Why is plastic a good choice for a raincoat?
questions.explanation: Plastic does not let water through, so it keeps you dry in the rain.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A saucepan has a metal base and a plastic handle. Why is the handle made of plastic and not metal?
choices: Plastic is a poor conductor of heat
Plastic is a better conductor of heat
questions.explanation: Plastic does not let heat travel through it easily, so the handle stays cool enough to hold.
